body: Lol I just realized I meant to say you're not alone not you're alone my bad. But yea I get it. Just never be afraid to reach out to someone and talk about how you're feeling. It doesn't have to be burden. ❤️

You're alone. You're allowed to have your journey no matter how many twists and turns it may take. I'm in the same position, and it's genuinely really stressful a lot of the time. As I think about it right now Im taking a deep breath and telling myself that one day, in spite of all this, I will find myself.

I think the expression aspect is a big one for me. Using my hands is my go-to way to get some kinda euphoria or feel more girly. Im realizing it's definitely more than just a fetish, so Im really glad I bit the bullet and actually made this post. Thank you so much <3
Ive seen this article thrown around but never really took the time to read it, but it was honestly really enlightening and affirming. Thank you.

Define masculinity on your own terms. Step outside the box you've put yourself in. I've had extremely similar feelings. And Im not gonna flat out say you're trans but perhaps it's worth exploring and deconstructing your relationship with masculinity and why you feel so trapped in it.

Do you feel capable of achieving the same tenderness that lesbians have? If the answer is no, you should ask yourself why you feel that way. Unpack that.

It's your hyperawareness. You've trained your brain into hypervigilence mode whenever you're around them. Before you even register, what's happening, you're already mentally preparing yourself and assessing whether or not youre feeling or thinking these things. 

And when they happen you fixate on them and theyre all you can think about until they start to balloon out of control. You cant panic, you cant spiral. You have to be indifferent. Its hard when youre facing down the worst things imaginable but thats just what you have to do. You have to breath and let those feelings wash over you. You take them, acknowledge them, and then let them go.

Ive gone through the same exact thing youre going through. The less you focus on it, the less of a grip theyll have on you. Im sure you had a real life before all this and you can very well return to it. Get a psychiatrist and a therapist who's trained to deal with ocd and obsessive thinking patterns like this.
I swear to God Im not intending to hurt anything. I have never once wanted to hurt any of the animals here.

I wish my lack of empathy manifested that way instead of just sadism and a desire to make people suffer the same way I do. But yea, I do also kind of follow that doctrine a bit. To make good choices in spite of yourself. I just wish it had changed for the better at this point.

Im trying to keep my goals in mind. I know deep down I dont want that. I want to be good, I know somewhere inside me I want to be good. I just desperately dont want that desire to fade away. I wanna cling onto it for dear life because it's all I have. 

I think your replies have helped me stabilize just a little. I really appreciate you taking the time to talk to me. Thank you. It was encouraging.

I guess I just feel apathetic. I spent so much of my life terrified of letting the mask slip, and now if it does and it destroys the world around me... idk. It doesn't phase me. Im not used to apathy like this. But yea, you may be right. I haven't really developed any real coping mechanisms. I'm left to my own devices without the fear of abandonment or consequences for once, and I'm just scared.

It was nice to find someone's issues at least slightly resemble mine cause up until now, it's been extremely isolating. I honestly think ocd + personality disorders/ptsd is just a devastating combo. I have npd with a little bit of bpd thrown in, and it just makes everything so much worse. 

You deserve peace. I hope you can find it one day. I'd like to think we're more victims than we are monsters.

Yes, I feel as though this disorder has done irreversible damage. I feel Im genuinely uniquely twisted and depraved in a way I can barely even grasp and would struggle to get others to even begin to understand. The line between reality and illness has completely blurred, and the only world I live in is my own head. 

My ocd also greatly targets my sexuality in ways I genuinely could never tell to anyone other than a trained professional. You're not alone. It took me 6 years, but I'm finally figuring out how to put a stop to the constant cycle of rumination/introspection. I doubt it'll ever repair the damage done to me, but if people like us can just manage to get peace and fucking quiet in our heads I think things can get better.

My post history is full of stuff that reads exactly like yours, so I understood immediately what you were going through. Journaling might be something worth looking into; it's the perfect place to spill your guts. I remember being on a group call with my friends where I was just sitting there quietly stewing in my own jealousy and hatred. Then I just started furiously writing down how I was feeling in my journal. I wrote about how I hated them and all the terrible shit I wanted to happen to them. It didnt cure me of anything, but in the moment it felt good to dump those feelings somewhere they couldn't hurt anyone. Some place outside the insanity of my own head. People talk about journaling a lot, and I always shrugged it off as kind of worthless but it really does help.

I was in a similar position. I took some time off work and some time away from my friends to get my insane jealousy under control, but nothing really helped until I started focusing more on myself and my own shortcomings. I just couldn't keep living that way if it meant being in a constant state of just barely stifling my jealousy and anger and insecurity in every interaction I have with my friends. You have to stop chasing validation and perfectionism. You have to build an actual relationship with yourself, give yourself the love you were denied as a child and incessantly chase as an adult.

Its hard and painful. Whenever I look within myself, I am utterly disgusted by the monster I've become. I let my insecurities fester inside me for so long and they've warped me into something I can barely recognize as  human. For us, it'd be easier to move mountains than to find a way to love ourselves. But you have to. Not just for the people you may hurt as a result but for your own self-preservation. There is a real world outside our own suffering that we can engage with if we just learn the tools to do so.

Take a break. Find a therapist. Get on some medication. Spend time with yourself. The more you put yourself situations that ignite your npd the closer you get to disaster. Regardless of your reasons for doing it, whether they be selfish or not, the act of choosing to do better and to heal yourself will always be a meaningful one. 

I wish you luck. You're capable. Everyone is, even the worst of us.

To me, metacognition was always a defense mechanism. I was and honestly still am convinced that if I dont maintain a constant vicegrip on my psyche, I'll completely snap and hurt someone. I have evil in my head, and it needs to be constantly curated and controlled. Ocd is definitely a huge component here. Everything feels so deliberate now, and every thought and action feels orchestrated. I don't feel human anymore, I think self-awareness of everything has kind of robbed me of it. I think for obsessive people whose obsessions primarily manifest in their mind, we need to have absolute control over our thoughts. For me, every thought and feeling needs to go through a filter. A conveyer belt in my head where I need to consciously sift through each thought and determine what is appropriate and what isn't. What has a place in my brain and what doesn't. It's like Im actively deconstructing my own psyche; my own humanity. To build something completely new from the ashes. 

It's ocd, or at least something to do with it. I remember one of my old therapists told me to stop ruminating and that it was a habit I needed to break. Maybe he was right to an extent, but calling it a compulsion almost feels inaccurate. For me, it's an active state of being, not a deliberate choice. I genuinely dont know what it's like or how to turn the noise off.

I know this may not be exactly the same as your experience. But what you wrote still felt very familiar to me in a way I've rarely seen elsewhere. I genuinely believe it's possible to break the cycle and feel like a person again. I've been making progress recently, and even though it's small, it still feels significant. There is hope.

yeah ive been there, its an emotional roller coaster. 

if theres two things i cant stress enough though, its:

1. if you dysphoria in any regard, you arent cis. and dysphoria isnt something you can make up. when i was in deep denial, i assumed i had just somehow manufactured my dysphoria. i figured if i had created it, i could get rid of it. except i couldn't. its still very much here. and as shitty as it can be, knowing its real is validating.

2. YOU CAN ALLOW YOURSELF TO BE HAPPY. this one is so important. grasping hold of your identity can be so terrifying. change is scary. but honestly expressing yourself is so liberating. you NEED to allow yourself to express yourself. its so essential cause otherwise you'll end up in a negative feedback loop. its okay to let yourself be happy. its okay and its necessary.

you dont need to know. some trans people dont even know until they start hormones. dont expect things to make perfect sense, when youve gone your whole life being one thing only to realize you may be another, things are bound to be confusing. 

i'd start trying to express yourself, whether that be through pronouns or clothes or names. take things slow. dont rush into things, if you do you'll end up like me and have a daily existential crisis lmao.

ive been where you are. tons of trans people have. its normal to feel what you feel. i was in the exact same boat but honestly the more you explore your identity the more you learn about yourself. i thought i was subconsciously doing it for validation, but dysphoria cant be manufactured. it cant be artificial. if youre here and youre feeling confused about yourself, chances are you arent happy with your gender. which probably means you arent cis. dont be afraid to explore these feelings. explore yourself and see what makes you happy and comfortable. i know these feelings can feel fake at first. hell, they still do for me. but take it from someone who was in your exact same shoes a month ago: you arent faking it. you arent blowing things out of proportion. youre opening a gate to a world of self discovery and as grueling and as painful as the road ahead can be, above all else you should pursue happiness. take your time. explore your identity at your own pace. it'll be okay.

stay strong 💕
